Subject: Zodiac compute profile + target SLOs

Hi Jasmine —

Thanks again for the demo. Priya and I pulled together a short compute profile (attached) and a suggested SLO we want to hit for production: p95 <= 350ms for chat responses (up to 1.5k tokens per request, average 400). We expect a steady-state of ~80k tokens/min in month one, ramping to 320k tokens/min by month six.

A few asks for your sizing check:
- What dedicated slab would you recommend to match p95=350ms with ~20% headroom for bursts?
- If we quantize to 4-bit and use prefix KV caching for context reuse, how much does that change GPU requirements?
- Any additional latency/availability caveats we should bake into the contract?

Attached: zodiac_compute_profile.xlsx (token distribution + sample traces), latency samples.

Cheers,
Samir Rao
Head of Platform, Zodiac AI

From: jasmine_liu@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Zodiac compute profile + target SLOs

Samir / Priya —

Thanks for the profile. I reviewed the token distribution and sample traces. High-level takeaways below; fuller numbers in the attachment (zodiac_compute_profile_reckoner.xlsx) that I’ll send after internal sizing sign-off.

Summary answers:
1) Baseline SKU: H100-80GB (FP16) slab with 4 GPUs per pod gives the best latency headroom for long-context chat. For your initial ramp (80k tokens/min, avg 400 tokens/request ~200 reqs/min), we estimate a single 4xH100 slab can sustain ~130k tokens/min at p95~300ms (warm KV cache). To hit p95=350ms with ~20% burst headroom, recommended reserved capacity for month one = 1 slab (4 GPUs) + 1 burst slab on demand.

2) Quantization and KV cache impact: moving to 4-bit quantized kernels reduces per-token compute ~1.7x (approx) but increases memory pressure for KV cache; with quant + optimized kernels we project a single 4xH100 slab to cover ~200k tokens/min warm. However cold-starts (cache miss on new conversations) will still spike latency — plan for request-level caching plus a small cold-start buffer (we recommend 25% additional capacity for cold tails).

3) SLA caveats and suggested terms:
- p95 measurement: include 95th percentile measured on end-to-end response generation excluding streaming tail (agree on measurement windows).
- Warm vs cold: define warm-cache baseline and a separate cold-start latency SLA or an allowed burst window.
- Fallback policy: automatic fallback to quantized Llama2-chat-v2 (compatible model variant) on capacity pressure. Include explicit throughput and latency expectations for fallback model.

Requested next steps:
- Ben: can you validate the GPU packing and autoscale/burst policy numbers below?
- Laura: finance — can you review term impact if they require 2x reserved slabs from day-one (discount ask)?

I’ll follow up with a spreadsheet of token/sec per SKU and the proposed clause language for the SLA.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter@redwood.com

Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Zodiac compute profile + target SLOs

Folks —

I validated the rough math and ran a quick slab simulation using our latency model. Key numbers (rounded):
- Workload assumptions used: avg request 400 tokens, 1.5k max, expected token mix matches attachment. Mixed decode model = 80% short responses, 15% mid, 5% long.

- GPU SKU options (warm KV cache):
  * 4xH100 (FP16): ~200k tokens/min sustained at p95=320ms with 20% burst headroom (quant disabled).
  * 4xH100 (4-bit kernels): ~340k tokens/min sustained at p95=340ms with 20% headroom (note slightly higher p95 due to kernel variability).
  * 8xA100 (FP16) across two pods: ~180k tokens/min sustained at p95=350ms (worse tail due to inter-pod variance).

- Cold-start tail: expect p95 to degrade by ~1.6x on cold sessions for long (>1k token) requests. We recommend a cold-buffer policy: keep one hot slab for warm traffic and a standing 25% warm-extra capacity reserved for cold tails during peak windows.

Recommendation for Month 1 (ramp to 80k tokens/min):
- Reserve: 1x 4-GPU H100 slab (baseline).
- Burst: on-demand 1x 4-GPU H100 (auto-scale policy).
- Cold-buffer: ensure 25% additional headroom in autoscaler config (policy tag: "cold-buffer").

For Month 6 ramp (320k tokens/min):
- Reserve: 2x 4-GPU H100 slabs + autoscale for bursts (or 1x 4-GPU H100 quantized + 1x 4-GPU H100 FP16 to balance quality vs cost).

Open items:
- Laura: pricing tiers and discount if they commit to 6-month reserved 2-slab contract.
- Samir/Priya: confirm tolerance for fallback model (quantized Llama2-chat) and whether 4-bit quality tradeoffs are acceptable.

Attachments: I’m attaching the simulation output (zodiac_slab_simulation.csv) — see the linked Drive doc in the thread.

-ben
Ben Carter
Head of Dedicated Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Zodiac compute profile + target SLOs — Final reckoning and next steps

Samir / Priya —

Summarizing agreed sizing approach and proposed contract language to put into the draft SLA:

Sizing snapshot (conservative):
- Month 1 (80k tokens/min): Reserve 1x 4xH100 slab (baseline FP16); autoscale to 1x additional 4xH100 slab for bursts. This configuration provides warm p95 ~= 300ms and 20% burst headroom.
- Month 6 (320k tokens/min): Recommend reserved 2x 4xH100 slabs OR 1x quantized 4xH100 + 1x FP16 4xH100 to balance cost and quality. Provision autoscale to add 1x slab for extreme bursts.

SLA language snippets to include in the contract:
- Measurement: p95 computed on completed response times measured at Redwood edge over 30-day rolling window; separate metrics reported for warm-cache and cold-start windows.
- Warm baseline: Redwood guarantees p95 <= 350ms for warm-cache traffic given the reserved slab counts defined in the schedule; allowed deviation during announced maintenance windows.
- Cold-start window: Redwood will provide best-effort cold-start p95 targets and maintain a documented cold-buffer policy (25% capacity) during peak hours; cold tails are excluded from billing SLA credits but will be monitored for regressions.
- Fallback: On capacity shortage Redwood will route to an agreed fallback model; fallback performance and quality expectations must be documented and signed off in addendum A.

Action items:
- Samir/Priya: confirm fallback acceptance (yes/no) and whether you want fallback quality tests run against your evaluation prompts.
- Laura: propose contract discount curve for 6- and 12-month reserved slab commitments.
- Ben: finalize simulation file and attach the per-minute token maps for their traces.

I’ve attached the spreadsheet with the conservative per-SKU token estimates and a short one-pager for legal (zodiac_sla_draft_v2.pdf). If that all looks good, we’ll produce a redlined SLA that includes the measurement windows and the addendum describing fallback behavior.

Thanks — appreciate the fast turnaround.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
